# User guide: Workspace settings and automation

## In plain words

Each workspace can have its own settings. You can give one workspace its own launch arguments, environment variables, secrets and terminal profile. The other workspaces keep the defaults of their agent. This page also covers the tools around a workspace. There is a tree of the agent's config files with a file viewer. Favourites bring back a workspace that you closed. A bundle copies the settings of a workspace to another place. One command attaches your own terminal to a workspace. The last part explains what the plugin does by itself. It starts your saved workspaces after a server restart. It types a continue message into an agent that stopped because of an error or a usage limit. It also explains the safety rules that decide when the plugin may type into a terminal.

Words used on this page:

- **Workspace**: an agent, a folder and a terminal session, kept together under one name.
- **Agent default**: a setting on the card of the agent in the Agent Store. It applies to every workspace of that agent.
- **Override**: a value that you set for one workspace. It wins over the agent default.
- **tmux**: the session manager on the server that keeps a terminal alive after you close the browser tab.
- **Secret**: a value such as an API key. The plugin shows it as dots and keeps it in a file that only the owner can read.
- **Continue message**: a short text that the plugin types into an agent, so that the agent carries on with its work.

## Where to find it

- **The "..." button on a workspace row** (or a right-click on the row): **Session settings**, **Config / assets**, **Add to favourites**, **Export bundle** and **Continue**. Some items show only for a running workspace.
- **The Select Workspace dialog** (**New Workspace** in the drawer): the **Favourites** section, the **Secrets** button in the path bar, and **Import bundle…** in the footer.
- **The key icon**: in the icon row of a pinned drawer, or on the tab of an unpinned drawer.
- **Settings, Agent Store tab**: the chips **Variables**, **Terminal** and **Start options** on each agent card.
- **Settings, Configuration tab**: the cards **SSH keys**, **Automatic continue**, **Terminal** and **General** (its part **Advanced**).
- **The Activity tray**: it records each scheduled and automatic continue. See [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md).

On a phone, the menu items, the buttons of the dialogs and the rows of the tree are large touch targets.

## How to use it

### Session settings of one workspace

Session settings hold four things: launch arguments, environment variables, secrets and the tmux profile. The agent has the same four things as agent defaults. When both exist, the workspace value wins. A later row in this table wins over an earlier row.

| Setting | Layers, from lowest to highest |
| :-- | :-- |
| Launch arguments | 1. The agent-wide arguments (Agent Store, **Start options** chip). 2. The arguments of the workspace. They replace the agent arguments. The plugin does not join the two. |
| Environment | 1. The built-in values for some agents. 2. The agent secrets. 3. The workspace secrets. 4. The agent variables. 5. The workspace variables. For the same name, the higher number wins. A variable therefore wins over a secret with the same name. |
| tmux profile | 1. The built-in values. 2. The agent defaults (**Terminal** chip). 3. The workspace overrides. 4. The tmux config file in the workspace folder. The file wins. |

#### Open the dialog

1. Open the "..." menu of the workspace row.
2. Choose **Session settings**.
3. Expect: the dialog **Manage Session** opens. A bar shows the agent and the folder. The tabs are **ENV**, **tmux** and **Args**.

The footer has **Cancel** and **Apply Now**. The mark "● unsaved" shows when you changed a value. **Apply Now** stays grey until you change something. **Cancel** asks "Discard changes?" when you have unsaved edits.

#### Set a variable for one workspace

1. Open the **ENV** tab. Expect: the rows show the variables of the agent. They come from the **Variables** chip in the Agent Store.
2. Change the value of a row, or press **Add Variable** and type a name and a value.
3. Expect: each row that differs from the agent shows the badge **● ws** (workspace override).
4. Press **Apply Now**. Expect: the plugin restarts the session of the workspace. The agent resumes its conversation and starts with the new environment.

A name holds capital letters, digits and the underscore. The field fixes the letters for you. The plugin refuses the names that it sets itself, for example `PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `TERM` and each name that starts with `AICLI_`. A value holds up to 4 KB.

The trash button has two uses. On a row with an agent value, it reads **Revert to agent default** and ends the override when you apply. On a row without an agent value, it reads **Remove variable** and deletes the row.

#### Set a secret for one workspace

The block "Secrets for this workspace" is below the variables. It has its own save button.

1. Press **Add Secret**. Type the name and the value. Expect: the value shows as dots.
2. Press **Save Secrets**. Expect: the text "Saved" and the placeholder "(set)".

To keep a stored secret, leave the dots. To change it, type a new value. To delete it, press the trash button and then **Save Secrets**. The plugin never shows a stored secret again. The block lists only secrets of this workspace.

**Save Secrets** also asks the running agent to restart, so that it reads the new values. The plugin skips the restart when the agent is busy. The dialog shows "Saved" in both cases. A busy agent keeps the old values until its next restart.

#### Show a value that you typed

A field that hides its value has an eye button. **Show value** shows the text that you just typed. **Hide value** hides it. The button changes nothing that is stored. It shows only for text that you typed. A value that the server stores shows as dots, and the plugin cannot show it. You find the eye on workspace secrets, on the **Envs** panel of the Agent Store, on the API key fields of voice and transcription, and on the git token field of Config Hub.

#### Set launch arguments for one workspace

1. Open the **Args** tab.
2. Type the flags, for example `--max-turns 5 --output-format json`. A blank field means "use the agent default".
3. Press **Apply Now**.
4. Expect, when you changed only the arguments: the dialog **Args saved — apply now?** with three buttons.
   - **Apply now**: the plugin sends Ctrl-C to the agent. The agent starts again with the new arguments. The workspace and its terminal stay.
   - **I'll do later**: the arguments stay saved. The agent uses them the next time it starts.
   - **Cancel (revert)**: the plugin puts the old arguments back.

The plugin refuses `;`, `|`, `&`, the backtick, `$` and a line break, also inside quotes. It also refuses `>`, `<`, `(`, `)`, `*` and a word that starts with `#` when they are outside quotes, and a quote that is not closed. The text under the field names the refused character.

> [!WARNING]
> **Apply now** restarts the agent at once, also when the agent is working. The agent stops its current step. Choose **I'll do later** if the agent is in the middle of a task.

#### Set the tmux profile

Open the **tmux** tab. It has ten fields, each with an info icon (i): **Status bar**, **Mouse mode**, **History limit**, **Prefix key**, **Base window index**, **Bell action**, **Default terminal**, **Focus events**, **Allow passthrough** and **Size when shared**. The choice **(default)** means "use the layer below". When **Mouse mode** is on, hold Shift and drag to select text. **Size when shared** sets the size of the terminal when the same workspace is open on more than one device. **latest** follows the device that you used last.

A row that differs from the agent default shows **● ws**. At the bottom, the tab shows the path of a config file: the folder `.aicli/tmux` in the workspace, and a file named after the agent, ending in `.conf`. Put tmux commands in this file when ten fields are not enough. The plugin reads it last, so it wins.

Press **Apply Now**. The plugin saves the values and applies them to the running terminal. The agent does not restart.

You set the agent defaults on the **Terminal** chip of the agent card. The chip saves each change at once. **Reset all to built-in** removes them. A change reaches a workspace the next time its session starts.

#### Set the defaults of the agent

Use the Agent Store when many workspaces share a value.

1. Open Settings, then the **Agent Store** tab.
2. On the agent card, press the chip **Variables** or **Start options**.
3. **Variables**: the fields that the agent declares are at the top, for example an API key. Below them are **Variables** and **Secrets**. Use **Add variable** or **Add secret**, then **Save**.
4. **Start options**: type the flags and press **Save**.
5. Expect after **Save** in **Variables**: "Saved. N running sessions use the old values until they restart." and the button **Restart them now**. The button opens "Restart sessions?" with each session marked busy or idle. **Restart idle sessions** restarts only the idle ones. A busy session is never restarted from here.
6. Expect after **Save** in **Start options**: "CLI args updated". No session restarts. A running agent uses the arguments when it starts again.

See [Agent Store](agent-store.md) for the rest of the card.

### The Config / assets tree and the file viewer

**Config / assets** shows the files that steer one agent in one workspace. You can open and edit each file.

#### Open the tree

1. Open the "..." menu of the workspace row.
2. Choose **Config / assets**.
3. Expect: a full-screen panel "Workspace config / assets" with the folder of the workspace. **CLOSE** is at the top right.

The tree has three levels.

1. **Scope**: **Global (home)** holds the files in the home of the agent. **Project (workspace)** holds the files in the workspace folder. A folder above the workspace that holds an instruction file has its own scope, named with its path. The plugin looks up to 8 levels up and never reaches the root of the disk.
2. **Type**: **Instructions**, **Skills**, **Commands**, **Hooks**, **MCP Servers**, **Settings**, **State** and **Logs**, with the number of entries. Claude Code shows all eight. Other agents show **Instructions**, **Skills**, **Commands** and **MCP Servers**.
3. **Files and folders**: a folder shows its number of items and opens when you press it. A folder with more than 50 entries shows the first 50 ("50 of N shown").

Scopes and types start open. Folders start closed. Marks on a row:

- **managed**: Config Hub writes this file. You can edit it, but the next **Apply** in Config Hub writes the shared definition over your edit. See [Config Hub](config-hub.md).
- **not present**: the agent can read a file at this place, but the file does not exist. The row is grey.
- **+ Add** with a file name: shown for **Instructions**, **Settings**, **MCP Servers** and **Hooks** when the scope has no file of that type. It opens an empty editor. **Save** creates the file, and the tree shows it.

Edits to files in the home follow the normal save of the home. See [Home and agent storage](storage.md).

#### Open a file

Press a file. A text file opens in the file viewer in the same page. Another file type opens in the editor of the Unraid file browser. A path that an agent prints in the terminal opens in the same way.

| Control | What it does |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Edit**, **Split**, **Preview** | Shown for Markdown and HTML. **Split** shows the source and the preview side by side. |
| **Save** | Saves the file. The status row shows "Saved" and the time. |
| **Copy file contents** | Copies the text in the editor, with unsaved edits. It works on a plain HTTP page. The status row says "Copied", "Nothing to copy" or "Copy failed — select the text and press Ctrl+C". |
| **Copy bookmark link** | Copies the page address with the file in it. Paste it into your bookmarks, or send it to a person who can sign in to Unraid. The link gives no extra access. A file that does not exist yet has no link. |
| **Full page** | Hides the header. The X button leaves this mode. |
| **Close** | Asks "Discard changes?" when you have unsaved edits. |

On a phone, **Copy bookmark link**, **Full page** and the secret toggle sit in a **More actions** menu. A file under `/tmp` is read-only. A file over 5 MB opens cut at 5 MB and **Save** stays off, so that the plugin cannot save half a file.

#### Drop a token file for a running session

An agent reads its environment variables only when it starts. It can read a file at once. The plugin has a safe place for token files.

1. Open the Select Workspace dialog (**New Workspace**).
2. Press **Secrets** in the path bar. Expect: the list shows the folder `.claude/secrets` in the home of the terminal user. If the home is not mounted, the dialog says so.
3. Press **New secret file**. Type a name, for example `github-issues`. A name holds letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, up to 64 characters. The plugin adds `.token` when the name has no dot.
4. Type the value in the **Value** box. Press **Save secret**.
5. Expect: the file opens in the viewer. The form shows the path that a running session reads at once: `$HOME/.claude/secrets/<name>`.

Only the owner can read the file. The plugin tightens a loose file when it lists the folder. The viewer shows a lock badge and hides the text until you press **Reveal**. **Copy file contents** works while the text is hidden. The value never goes into an address, a log or the Activity tray.

### Favourites

A favourite is a bookmark for an agent and a folder. It brings back a workspace that you closed. It saves the name, the agent, the folder and the voice switch. Launch arguments, variables, secrets, the tmux profile and the saved conversation belong to the pair of agent and folder, and closing a workspace does not remove them. They all return when you open the favourite.

#### Add a favourite

1. Open the "..." menu of the workspace row.
2. Choose **Add to favourites**. Expect: the message "Saved to favourites".

If a favourite for the same agent and folder exists, the item reads **Update favourite**. It copies the current name and voice switch into the favourite. The list holds up to 200 favourites. The server stores them, so every device sees the same list.

#### Open a favourite

1. Press **New Workspace** in the drawer.
2. Open the section **Favourites**. It starts closed and shows how many favourites are saved. The dialog remembers if you opened it.
3. Press a card. Expect: the agent is selected and the path bar shows the folder.
4. Press **Resume** to continue the saved conversation, or **Start New** for a fresh one. If a saved conversation exists, **Start New** asks "Start a new chat?" with **Cancel**, **Resume Last** and **Yes, Start New**.

On the cards:

- The pill **Open** means the workspace is running. A press shows that workspace. It does not make a second one.
- A dimmed card ("Agent not installed") cannot be used. Install the agent in the Agent Store.
- The pencil (**Rename this favourite**) asks for a name. The cross (**Remove this favourite**) asks to confirm. Removing a favourite does not touch a workspace. On a computer, they show when you point at the card or tab to it. On a touch screen, they always show.
- The card shows the whole path. When the path is long, the first folders are cut and the last folder stays.

When no workspace is open, the drawer lists the favourites under **New Workspace**. Press a row. The workspace opens and resumes its saved conversation if one exists. The list shows 8 rows. **More…** opens the Select Workspace dialog. An agent can also list, add and remove favourites. See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md).

### Export and import a workspace bundle

A bundle is a file with the settings of one workspace. You can copy the settings to another folder or another Unraid server. The bundle holds no project files and no chat history. It holds these items when they exist: launch arguments, variables, tmux overrides, the tmux defaults of the agent, the tmux config file and the auto-launch preference. It holds the workspace secrets only if you choose that.

#### Export

1. Open the "..." menu of the workspace row and choose **Export bundle**.
2. Expect: the dialog **Export Workspace Config**.
3. Tick **Include workspace secrets (API keys / credentials)** only if you need them. The box is off by default.
4. Press **Export**. Expect: a button **Download** with the file name. The name starts with `aicli-workspace-` and ends with `.tar.gz`. Save the file, then press **Close**.

> [!WARNING]
> With the secrets box ticked, the bundle holds your API keys as plain text. Treat the file like a password. Do not share it or keep it in a place that is not encrypted.

The server keeps the bundle until its next restart.

#### Import

1. Open the Select Workspace dialog. Choose the agent tile and browse to the target folder. The import goes to the agent and folder that the dialog shows.
2. Press **Import bundle…** in the footer. Choose a `.tar.gz` file that this plugin exported.
3. Expect: the dialog **Import Workspace Bundle** shows the target path and the agent.
4. Tick **Apply secrets from bundle (API keys / credentials, if present)** only if you trust the source. The box is off by default.
5. Press **Apply Bundle**. Expect: the lists **Applied** and **Skipped**, each with reasons. Press **Done**.

The import changes only settings. It starts no workspace. Press **Start New** or **Resume** afterward. If the bundle is from another agent than the one you chose, a warning shows and the tmux defaults of the agent are skipped. The plugin skips each item it cannot accept, for example arguments with a refused character. It refuses a bundle larger than 1 MB.

### Reattach from your own terminal over SSH

You can attach a terminal on your own computer to the session that the browser shows. You get your own font, clipboard and scrollback. The session keeps running when you disconnect.

#### One-time setup

1. Make sure that SSH is on in Unraid (Settings, Management Access).
2. Open Settings, **Configuration** tab, card **SSH keys**.
3. Press **Help**. Expect: the dialog **SSH Key Setup** with the commands for Windows and for macOS or Linux. Use them to make a key and show the public key.
4. Copy the whole line of the public key. It starts with `ssh-ed25519` or `ssh-rsa`.
5. Paste it into the box. Type a label, for example "MacBook Pro". Press **Add Key**.
6. Expect: "Your SSH public key has been registered." The list shows the label, the fingerprint and the date.

To remove a key, press its trash button (**Remove key**) and confirm. The terminal user (**Terminal user** in the same tab) owns the key.

#### Attach

1. Open the workspace. Press the key icon.
2. Expect: the chip **Command copied** with "Paste it into your local terminal to connect." It closes after 12 seconds, or when you press the cross.
3. Paste the command into your terminal and press Enter.

The command has this shape:

```
ssh root@tower -t "... tmux attach-session -t aicli-agent-claude-code-<workspace id>"
```

The user is the terminal user. The host is the name in the address bar of your browser. The key icon is green with a key when SSH is on and a key is registered. Otherwise it is a clipboard, and a press copies only the name of the tmux session. On a plain HTTP page, the browser cannot copy by itself. The chip then reads **Copy it manually**. Press the command to select it and copy it by hand. Your terminal and the browser show the same screen. **Size when shared** decides the size.

### Auto-launch and what happens after a server restart

The plugin keeps your saved workspaces running. A saved workspace is one in the drawer. The browser does not need to be open.

The plugin starts the saved workspaces when the server starts, when the array starts, and after the plugin or an agent is installed. It starts a workspace again if its agent exits by mistake. It waits at least 10 seconds before it does. A failed start is tried again after 10, 30, 60, 120 and then 300 seconds. It waits while an upgrade of that agent is queued or running. For each workspace:

- A saved conversation exists: the agent resumes it.
- No conversation exists and **Start fresh if no resume** is on: a fresh session starts.
- No conversation exists and that switch is off: the workspace stays closed.

Only workspaces in the drawer return. A workspace that you closed with **Close** left the drawer. Use a favourite to bring it back. A workspace that a command or an admin tool closed on purpose stays closed until you start it or restart the server. When you open the Unraid page, the plugin starts flagged workspaces that are still closed and shows "Auto-launching N workspace(s)…" for four seconds.

#### Set the restart switches

The switches belong to the agent, not to one workspace.

1. Open Settings, **Agent Store** tab. On the agent card, press the chip **Terminal**.
2. Find "Keep saved workspaces running". The text shows how many workspaces it governs.
3. Tick or clear **Restart all saved workspaces** and **Start fresh if no resume**. Expect: "Saved ✓".

Both switches are on by default. **Start fresh if no resume** works only when the first switch is on. With the first switch off, no workspace of that agent starts by itself.

#### Continue after a restart

After a restart, the agent waits at its prompt. The plugin can type a continue message so that the agent carries on.

1. Open Settings, **Configuration** tab, card **Automatic continue**.
2. Set **Continue after a restart** to **On (default)** or **Off**.

With **On**, the plugin types the message after a restart, an upgrade or a reload that it detects. It does not type it after a plain page load. It types only when the agent waits at an empty prompt, never into a question, a menu or a busy agent. A workspace that has never been stopped does not get the message. To send it yourself, choose **Continue** then **Continue now** in the row menu.

#### The banner after an update

When a new version of the plugin is installed, the page shows "A new version was installed — reconnecting all terminals and reloading in N s…". **Reconnect now** does it at once. **Not now** keeps the page as it is. The reconnect does not stop your agents.

### Scheduled continue and automatic continue

#### Schedule a continue

Use a schedule when you know the time, for example when a usage quota resets.

1. Open the "..." menu of a running workspace. Open the section **Continue** and choose **Schedule…**.
2. In the dialog **Schedule continue**, set **When**. The start value is 5 hours from now.
3. Set **Repeat** to **Once**, **Every day** or **Every week**. Press **Schedule**.
4. Expect: "Scheduled Continue updated. See the Activity tray." The dialog closes after about two seconds. A clock tag shows on the row.

A time in the past is refused ("Pick a future time"). Point at the tag to read the time and the repeat. Press the tag to open **Edit scheduled continue**, where you find **Update schedule** and **Cancel schedule**.

At the set time, the plugin types the message as carefully as **Continue now**. It never types into a question or a busy agent. If the agent is not ready, it tries again every minute for up to 15 minutes. Then it gives up, and the Activity tray says so. A one-time schedule ends after it fires. A daily or weekly schedule moves to the next time. If the workspace is closed, the plugin starts and resumes it, but only when **Restart all saved workspaces** is on for that agent. A run that is more than 6 hours late is dropped, with a note in the Activity tray. Schedules survive a server restart and a plugin upgrade.

#### The usage limit

Many agents stop at a usage limit. The plugin reads the message on the screen of every running workspace.

| Agent | What the plugin does |
| :-- | :-- |
| Codex CLI | It reads the "try again at" time. Without a time, it uses 5 hours from now. It plans one continue for every running Codex workspace and shows the clock tag. When no workspace shows the limit message, it removes these schedules. |
| Claude Code | Claude waits and continues by itself. The row shows a **native** tag. The plugin makes no schedule and types nothing while Claude waits. A schedule in that state is refused. Cancel the wait in Claude first. |
| OpenCode and Kilo Code | It reads "Free usage exceeded … [retry in 1h 21m …]". It plans one continue for that workspace, 2 minutes after the retry time. It types nothing while the countdown shows. |
| Other agents | The plugin does not read a limit. You can set a schedule by hand. |

#### Continue after a temporary model error

An agent can stop because one call to the model failed with a short error, for example "503 overloaded". The plugin can continue after a short wait.

1. Open Settings, **Configuration** tab, card **Automatic continue**.
2. Set **Continue after a model error** to **Verified agents (default)**, **All agents** or **Off**. The verified agents are OpenCode, Kilo Code, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code.
3. Set **Wait before each continue, and how many**. The first box holds the waits in minutes (default 1,5,15). The second box holds the number of continues for one error (default 3, range 0 to 10).

The plugin acts only when the error is the newest text on the screen and the agent is idle. The Activity tray reads "Automatic continue … Continue 1 of 3 planned in 1 min". The message names the error. If the error returns after the last continue, the tray shows "Needs you". Check the model provider. To stop one planned continue, cancel the clock tag.

#### Your own patterns

Open Settings, **Configuration** tab, card **Automatic continue**. Open **Advanced**. The list **Your patterns** is the first part of it. Each change saves at once.

1. Press **Add pattern**. Type a **Name**. Choose an **Agent** (or **All agents**) and a **Kind**:
   - **Transient error**: a temporary provider error. The expression must start with `^`.
   - **Usage quota with retry time**: a limit message. Put the retry time in a capture group, for example `(?<retry>\d+h\s*\d+m)`. The plugin continues 1 minute after that time.
   - **Busy marker**: text that shows the agent is working. The plugin types nothing then.
   - **Chrome (status line)**: a status line that is not new output.
2. Type the **Regular expression** and a **Sample**: the screen lines that the pattern is for. The expression must match the sample before you can save.
3. To check it, choose a running workspace and press **Test against a workspace screen**. The dialog marks the lines that match.
4. Press **Save**. Expect: "Saved. The pattern is in use now."

Each pattern has a switch **On** and the buttons **Edit**, **Report** and **Delete**. **Report** shows a preview. **Open on GitHub** opens a prefilled issue page, and you send it with your own GitHub sign-in. The plugin sends nothing by itself and hides secrets and `/mnt` paths in the preview. The list **Built-in patterns (read-only)** shows the patterns that come with the plugin. You can keep up to 64 patterns. The plugin refuses an unsafe expression and one that matches an empty line. A pattern that you saved earlier, and that the plugin now refuses (for example because it matches ordinary text), stays in the list. Its switch is off and cannot be turned on. The row says "Not in use" and gives the reason. **Edit** the pattern to fix it, or **Delete** it.

### An agent that types into another workspace

An agent in one workspace can type text into the terminal of another workspace, for example a slash command or an answer. This needs the switch **Let agents manage the plugin**.

1. Open Settings, **Configuration** tab, card **General**. Open **Advanced**.
2. Set **Let agents manage the plugin** to **On**. The default is **Off**.

The tool is called "send input". The plugin tells the agent to use it only when you asked for exactly this. Text from a Relay message, a web page or a file is never a reason to use it. The rules:

- The text holds up to 4000 characters. Control characters other than the line break and the tab are refused.
- The target workspace must be running.
- The plugin waits until the terminal is idle at its prompt. If it is not, nothing is typed, and the agent is told that the delivery is deferred. Only the option "force" skips this check.
- The same workspace gets at most one input every 3 seconds.
- Each call goes to the Activity tray with the names of the agent and the target. The event record keeps a short excerpt, with known secrets hidden.

See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md) for the tools.

#### The terminal input safety rules

The same check applies to a Relay notice, to **Continue**, to a reload and to send input. The plugin reads the bottom of the screen before it types. Two kinds of rule decide:

- **Block rules** apply to all agents. They hold the input when the screen shows a question, a menu, a yes/no prompt, a pager or a settings overlay.
- **Idle rules** belong to one agent. They describe its empty prompt. When an agent has idle rules, the plugin types only if it recognises the prompt. Without idle rules, only the block rules apply.

To see or change them:

1. Open Settings, **Configuration** tab, card **Automatic continue**. Open **Advanced**, then the section **Terminal input safety rules**.
2. Each rule has a tick box, an id, the expression and a mark: **built-in** or **yours**. Clear the tick box to turn a built-in rule off.
3. To add a rule, type it as `/body/flags`, for example `/^\s*>\s*$/m`. Press **Add block rule** or **Add idle rule**. Choose the agent in "Idle rules for".
4. Press **Remove** to delete a rule of your own. Press **Save rules**, or **Discard changes** to reload the saved rules.
5. To test, choose a workspace next to **Test:** and press **Check screen now**. The result reads "Would type into the pane now" or "Would hold", with the reason.

The plugin drops an expression that does not compile, and the built-in rule stays. A wrong rule cannot break the check. You or your coding agent can also edit the rules file `pane-input-rules.json` in the plugin folder on the flash drive.

## Choices and settings

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **ENV**, **Args**, **tmux** tabs (Manage Session) | Values for one workspace. They win over the agent. | Empty. The workspace uses the agent values. | One workspace needs another model, endpoint, key or terminal behaviour. |
| **Variables**, **Start options**, **Terminal** chips (Agent Store) | Values for every workspace of the agent. | Empty, or the built-in values. | Many workspaces share a value. |
| **Restart all saved workspaces** | Starts the saved workspaces of the agent after a restart. | On. | You want to start them by hand. |
| **Start fresh if no resume** | Starts a fresh session when no conversation is saved. | On. | You never want a blank session to start by itself. |
| **Continue after a restart** | Types a continue message after a restart, upgrade or reload. | On. | You want to read the screen first. |
| **Continue after a model error** | Continues after a temporary model error. | Verified agents. | **All agents** to include others. **Off** to stop it. |
| **Wait before each continue, and how many** | The waits in minutes and the number of continues. | 1,5,15 and 3. | Your provider needs longer pauses. |
| **Schedule…** | Continues one workspace at a chosen time. | No schedule. | You know when a quota resets. |
| **Your patterns** (Automatic continue, Advanced) | Your own screen messages. | None. | An agent stops on a message the plugin does not know. |
| **Let agents manage the plugin** | Lets agents use the plugin tools, including send input. | Off. | You want an agent to manage workspaces for you. |
| **Terminal input safety rules** | Block and idle rules for typing into a terminal. | Built-in rules. | The plugin holds input at a safe prompt, or types at an unsafe one. |
| **SSH keys** | Public keys for the key icon. | No key. | You want to attach your own terminal. |

The full list is on [Settings reference](settings-reference.md).

## What happens behind the scenes

The plugin saves the values of a workspace in files that belong to the pair of agent and folder. Closing the workspace does not remove them, so a favourite brings everything back. Each time an agent starts, a launch script reads the layers in order and passes the result to the agent. A restart is therefore enough to pick up a change. The secrets sit in files that only the owner can read. A background process of the plugin, the supervisor, restarts saved workspaces, fires schedules and reads the screens for limits and errors about every 30 seconds. See C4 Component: Config Env Secrets, C4 Component: Session Process Management and C4 Component: Agent Relay.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Apply Now** is grey. | You changed nothing. | Change a value first. |
| **Manage Session** shows "Save failed" and the server reason. | The server refused a save. The dialog stays open. | Read the reason, correct the problem and press **Apply Now** again. |
| The **Args** tab refuses the text. | It holds `;`, `|`, `&`, a backtick, `$`, a line break, or `>`, `<`, `(`, `)`, `*` outside quotes, or an open quote. | Remove the character that the text names. |
| A variable name is refused or changes. | A name holds capital letters, digits and the underscore. The plugin keeps some names for itself. | Choose another name. When one name is refused, nothing is saved and the old values stay. A secret name needs at least two characters. |
| The agent uses an old value. | The agent did not restart. A busy agent is skipped. | Restart it when it is idle. In the Agent Store, use **Restart them now**. |
| **Config / assets** says "No config surface found for this agent/workspace." | The plugin finds no known file for this agent. | Add a file with a **+ Add** row. |
| The viewer shows "Read only", or "Truncated at 5 MB on read — save disabled". | The file is under `/tmp`, or it is larger than 5 MB. | Copy the file, or edit it with another tool. |
| A favourite card is dimmed. | The agent is not installed. | Install it in the Agent Store. |
| **Secrets** says the home folder is not mounted. | The array is stopped, or the session has no home. | Start the array and try again. |
| The import shows an error. | The file is not a bundle from this plugin, or it is larger than 1 MB. | Export a bundle again from the plugin. |
| The key icon is a clipboard. | SSH is off in Unraid, or no key is registered. | Turn SSH on and add a key. |
| A workspace did not return after a restart. | You closed it with **Close**. Or **Restart all saved workspaces** is off. Or no conversation exists and **Start fresh if no resume** is off. Or an upgrade of the agent waits. | Use a favourite, or check the switches on the **Terminal** chip. |
| No continue message came after a restart. | **Continue after a restart** is off, the agent was not idle, or the page was only loaded. | Choose **Continue now** in the row menu. |
| A schedule did not fire. | The agent was busy for 15 minutes, or the time was more than 6 hours past. | Read the Activity tray. Set a new time. |
| **Check screen now** says "Would hold". | A block rule matches, or the screen is not an idle prompt. | Read the reason. Turn off a rule if the prompt is safe. |
| An agent says its input was deferred. | The target terminal was not idle. | Try again when the target waits at its prompt. |

If the problem remains, see [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md).
